q: 1. When analogy is drawn between Darcy's law for flow of water and Ohm's law for flow of current, what is analogous to the quantity of seepage?
explain: In the electrical analogy, seepage discharge corresponds to electrical current, head to voltage, and permeability to conductivity.

q: 2. An isobar is .............
options: a curve connecting points of equal vertical pressure
a point at which the net pressure is zero
a curve connecting points of equal pore water pressure
explain: An isobar (pressure bulb contour) is a curve connecting points of equal vertical stress increment below a loaded area.

q: 3. Consolidation theory was enunciated by .............
explain: Terzaghi developed the classical one-dimensional theory of consolidation, the foundation of modern soil mechanics.

q: 4. Consolidation is a process involving .............
explain: Consolidation is fundamentally the slow, time-dependent process of gradual pore water expulsion under sustained load.

q: 5. The law which states that the velocity of flow through porous medium is directly proportional to the hydraulic gradient is .............
explain: Darcy's law states that seepage velocity is directly proportional to hydraulic gradient, via v = Ki.

q: 6. Coefficient of permeability of a soil .............
options: increases with the decrease in temperature
increases with the increase in temperature
explain: Permeability increases with temperature because higher temperature reduces water's viscosity, allowing easier flow.

q: 7. Total pressure on the vertical face of a retaining wall of height h exerted by the retained earth weighting w per unit volume is
explain: Total active earth pressure force = area of the triangular pressure distribution = ½·Ka·w·h², where Ka = (1-sinφ)/(1+sinφ), giving (wh²/2)×Ka.

q: 8. Secondary consolidation is .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'caused by hydrostatic pressure'; secondary consolidation is more commonly attributed to creep (plastic readjustment) of soil structure.

q: 9. Rise of water table above the ground surface causes .............
options: equal increase in pore water pressure and total stress
equal increase in pore water pressure and effective stress
equal increase in total stress and effective stress
explain: Per the reference key, flooding above ground surface produces an equal rise in total stress and effective stress at a given point.

q: 10. The presence of organic matter in a soil will .............
explain: Per the reference key organic matter is marked as having no effect on permeability in this context.

q: 11. Choose the correct statement
options: confined aquifer is at upper level and unconfined aquiifer is at lower level under the ground
confined is temporary and unconfined is permanent under the ground
confined is unsaturated and unconfined is saturated under the ground
confined aquifer is at lower level and unconfined aquifer is at upper level under the ground
explain: Typically, an unconfined (water table) aquifer lies near the ground surface, while a confined (artesian) aquifer, trapped between impermeable layers, lies at a deeper level.

q: 12. Stability analysis shall be made considering .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'shear stresses'; the widely accepted standard practice is that slope stability analysis should use effective stresses.

q: 13. A clay deposit suffers a total settlement of 10 cm with one way drainage, then with two way drainage, it suffers a total settlement of .............
explain: Total (final) consolidation settlement depends only on the applied stress and soil compressibility, not on the drainage path — so it remains 10 cm; drainage path only affects the rate of settlement.

q: 14. The shear failure exhibited by loose sands is known as .............
explain: Loose sands compress and deform gradually under shear without a sharp peak, characteristic of plastic (ductile) failure.

q: 15. The value of Reynold's number for laminar flow through soil is .............
explain: Flow through soil is generally laminar as long as the Reynolds number stays below about 2,000, well within Darcy's law's valid range.

q: 16. The velocity of percolation is defined as .............
options: the discharge per unit of gross c/s area
the discharge per unit of net c/s area
the discharge per unit of total c/s area
explain: Percolation (seepage) velocity uses only the net (void) cross-sectional area available for actual water flow, not the gross soil area.

q: 17. Magnitude of capillary rise is more in .............
explain: Clay has the smallest pore sizes, producing the highest capillary rise due to greater surface tension effects in narrower channels.

q: 18. The height to which water can be lifted by capillarity is .............
options: independent of the atmospheric pressure value
depends upon the atmospheric pressure value
increases with decreasing diameter of the passage and is independent of the atmospheric pressure
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as depending on atmospheric pressure; the standard textbook fact is that capillary rise increases with decreasing pore diameter and is independent of atmospheric pressure.

q: 19. Piping in soils is due to .............
options: erosion of subsoil by high velocity of seepage flow
leakage of water through pipes laid in dams
passage of water through well-connected pores in soil
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as leakage through pipes in dams; the classical geotechnical definition of piping is progressive erosion caused by high-velocity seepage flow.

q: 20. Permeability of soil varies .............
options: inversely as square of grain size
explain: Per typical permeability relations (e.g., Hazen's formula), permeability is proportional to the square of the effective grain size.

q: 21. Physical properties of a permeant which influences the permeability are .............
explain: Permeability depends on the permeant fluid's unit weight and viscosity together, as seen in k = C.d^2.gamma/mu.

q: 22. Select the correct statement. The permeability is .............
options: directly proportional to unit weight, inversely proportional to viscosity
directly proportional to viscosity, inversely proportional to unit weight
directly proportional to both unit weight and viscosity
inversely proportional to both unit weight and viscosity
explain: Per the reference key this is marked as inversely proportional to both; the standard formula (k = C.d^2.gamma/mu) actually shows permeability directly proportional to unit weight and inversely proportional to viscosity.

q: 23. Units of co-efficient of permeability .............
explain: Per the reference key this is marked s^2/cm; the standard, correct unit for coefficient of permeability is actually cm/s (a velocity unit).

q: 24. The time required for full dissipation of pore water pressure will depend on .............
options: co-efficient of permeability of soil only
both thickness and co-efficient of permeability only
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'none of the above'; per consolidation theory (Tv = Cv.t/d^2), dissipation time depends on both layer thickness and permeability (via Cv).

q: 25. The ultimate strength of a loose and dense sand samples which are consolidated to the same value of effective stress will be .............
explain: At large strains (critical/ultimate state), both loose and dense sands consolidated to the same effective stress converge to the same ultimate strength.

q: 26. In a consolidated drained test on a normally consolidated clayey soil, the volume of the soil during the shearing will .............
explain: Normally consolidated clay contracts (decreases in volume) during drained shearing, unlike dilative over-consolidated clay.

q: 27. In the triaxial test, the intermediate principal stress will be equal to .............
options: average of major and minor principal stresses
explain: In a standard (axisymmetric) triaxial test, cell pressure acts equally on all lateral directions, so the intermediate principal stress equals the minor (confining) stress.

q: 28. The pressure exerted by water on the soil through which it percolates, is known as .............
explain: The drag force exerted by percolating (seeping) water on soil grains is termed seepage pressure.

q: 29. The equi-potential line in a seepage through a soil medium is defined as the .............
options: path of particles of water through a saturated soil mass
line connecting points of equal head of water
flow of movement of fine particles of soil
explain: An equipotential line connects all points in the seepage domain that share the same total head.

q: 30. The exit gradient of the seepage of water through a soil medium is the .............
options: ratio of total head to the length of seepage
ratio of the head loss to the length of seepage
explain: Exit gradient is defined as the head loss per unit length at the point where seepage exits the soil, i.e., head loss over seepage path length.

q: 31. The phenomenon in which a cohesion less soil loses all its shear strength and the soil particles have a tendency to move up in the direction of flow, is known as .............
explain: Boiling condition, quicksand, and quick condition are all terms used interchangeably for this loss of effective stress under upward seepage.

q: 32. Rise in the water table position upto the ground surface causes .............
explain: A rising water table increases pore water pressure and total stress at a given point, while effective stress typically decreases due to buoyant unit weight replacing dry/moist unit weight.

q: 33. Electrical analogy method is used to .............
options: find the depth to water table
find the water content in a soil
explain: The electrical analogy method uses the similarity between Darcy's and Ohm's laws to experimentally construct flow nets.

q: 34. The space factor of a flow net is defined as .............
explain: The space (shape) factor of a flow net is defined as the ratio of number of flow channels to number of equipotential drops, Nf/Nd.

q: 35. Find out the correct statement about shape factor .............
explain: The shape factor of a flow net depends only on geometry, not on the permeability value of the soil.

q: 36. The u/s face of an earth dam is .............
explain: The upstream (submerged) face of an earth dam, being in contact with reservoir water at constant head, acts as an equipotential line.

q: 37. The top flow line in the case of seepage flow through an earth dam has the shape of .............
explain: The phreatic (top flow) line through a homogeneous earth dam closely approximates a parabola (Casagrande's method).

q: 38. Flow through an earth dam is a case of .............
explain: Seepage through an earth dam has a free (phreatic) surface exposed to atmospheric pressure, characterizing unconfined flow.

q: 39. The pheriatic line is .............
options: the u/s face of the earth dam
d/s face of the earth dam
explain: The phreatic line is defined as the top flow line (free surface) of seepage through an earth dam.

q: 40. Quick sand is .............
options: a condition in which cohesion is decreased quickly
a sand which can act as a quick filter
condition in which cohesion less soil looses its shear strength due to upward flow of water
explain: Quicksand describes the condition where upward seepage force equals or exceeds submerged weight, eliminating effective stress and shear strength in cohesionless soil.

q: 41. The quantity of seepage in a soil is .............
options: directly proportional to the coefficient of permeability
inversely proportional to the coefficient of permeability
directly proportional to the uniformity coefficient of the soil
explain: By Darcy's law, seepage discharge is directly proportional to permeability (q = kiA).

q: 42. Flow net consists of a number of stream lines and equipotential lines which are .............
explain: Flow lines and equipotential lines in a flow net are drawn orthogonal (at right angles) to each other by construction.

q: 43. The seepage force in a soil is .............
explain: Seepage force acts in the direction of flow, which is perpendicular to the equipotential lines.

q: 44. The seepage force in soils at exit is proportional to .............
options: the head of water at d/s
the head of water at u/s
explain: Seepage force per unit volume at the exit point is directly proportional to the exit hydraulic gradient.

q: 45. Flow net is used for the determination of .............
explain: A flow net simultaneously allows determination of exit gradient, total seepage quantity, and pore/hydrostatic pressures at any point.

q: 46. Generally, when compacted the GW type of soils will be .............
explain: Even when well compacted, well-graded gravel (GW) retains interconnected voids large enough to remain pervious.

q: 47. A soil which is fully consolidated under the existing over burden pressure is known as .............
explain: A soil fully consolidated under its present overburden (with no excess pore pressure remaining) is defined as normally consolidated.

q: 48. Secondary consolidation of soil is due to the expulsion of .............
explain: Secondary consolidation involves slow expulsion of tightly bound (adsorbed) water and plastic readjustment of soil structure, distinct from primary consolidation's free water expulsion.

q: 49. The relationship between the time factor Tv, coefficient of consolidation Cv, the length of drainage path d, and time t is given by .............
explain: Time factor is defined as Tv = Cv.t/d^2, a dimensionless parameter combining consolidation coefficient, time, and drainage path length.

q: 50. The time factor for a particular degree of consolidation .............
options: depends upon the coefficient of consolidation
depends upon the distribution of initial excess hydrostatic pressure
explain: For a given degree of consolidation, the time factor Tv depends on the shape of the initial excess pore pressure distribution across the layer.
